title: Rain-matched years had less runoff after 2009 in 177 south-east Australian catchments, but tight climate matches failed
abstract: We test the south-east Australian runoff loss without a fitted rainfall-runoff curve. We match unique annual climate analogues within CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments. In 177 gauges, 2010-2021 runoff is lower than in rain-matched 1951-1996 years by 55.7 mm/year with AGCD rain (conditional 95% limits -78.7 to -35.8) and 39.8 with SILO (-59.8 to -20.3). Adding prior rain retains negative limits in smaller samples. However, the planned tight match on current rain, prior rain and temperature has no gauges with at least six pairs. Mean late-year coverage is only 12.0% and 12.6%. Wider preplanned climate limits retain 98 and 100 gauges. Their runoff differences are -46.2 [-78.1, -9.6] and -28.8 [-64.5, +6.9] mm/year. Thus the rain-conditioned loss needs no runoff curve, but the primary full-climate test is unsupported. The support map, two rain products and source dependence limit stronger attribution. We do not identify the water loss mechanism. Code, compatible annual inputs, hashes, plans, all pairs, mismatch audits, time-space draws and figures permit an offline repeat.

display.caption: Joint annual climate support is sparse under tight rain and temperature pair limits. Each curve uses all 177 eligible late-period gauges. Retention requires at least six unique pairs.

Runoff differences in supported climate years. Limits resample time blocks and spatial cells and recompute matching. Designs have different gauge populations. The primary tight full-climate test is undefined and is not shown as a runoff estimate.
